items.title: Section: The Four Classic Distortions — Mistaking Impermanence for Permanence, Suffering for Pleasure, Impurity for Purity, and Selflessness for Self

items.zh: 顛倒差別者，謂諸愚夫無所知曉，隨逐無明起不如理作意，於所緣境無常計常，取相而轉，是名想倒。如於無常計常，如是於苦計樂、於不淨計淨、於無我計我。此想顛倒，諸在家者能發心倒，一分出家者能發見倒。是名顛倒差別。此想顛倒復有差別。謂於四事邪取其相，是名想倒。若由如是等了相故，於境貪著，是名心
items.en:
Third, distortion; first, the primary sense; first, the explanation; first, distorted perception; first, mistaking the impermanent for permanent. Distortion names how ordinary, unlearned beings, following ignorance into improper attention, grasp what is impermanent as permanent, fixing perception on this mark — this is called distorted perception.
Second, extending this to the rest. As with mistaking the impermanent for permanent, so too with mistaking suffering for pleasure, impurity for purity, and selflessness for self.
Second, distorted mind and the rest. This distorted perception gives rise to distorted mind among householders, and to distorted view among a portion of renunciants. Second, the conclusion. This is called the distinction of distortion.
Second, the secondary sense; first, distorted perception. This distorted perception has a further distinction: wrongly grasping the characteristic of the four objects — this too is called distorted perception.
Second, distorted mind. When, through this same equal apprehension, craving attachment arises towards the object, this is called distorted mind.

items.title: Section: Distorted View Completes the Fourfold Error — And Freedom From Distortion Restores the Mind to Seeing Things As They Are

items.zh: 倒。若由如是等了相故，有執著者，於顛倒事堅執、忍可、開示、建立，是名見倒。無顛倒差別者，謂諸聰叡有所曉了，隨智慧明起如理作意，於所緣境，無常知無常，苦知是苦，不淨知不淨，無我知無我，正取相轉，是名想無顛倒、心無顛倒、見無顛倒。
items.en:
Third, distorted view. When, through this same equal apprehension, one clings to, endorses, teaches, and establishes these distorted matters as correct, this is called distorted view.
Fourth, freedom from distortion; first, the explanation. Freedom from distortion names how the genuinely intelligent, guided by wisdom's clarity into proper attention, correctly know the impermanent as impermanent, suffering as suffering, impurity as impurity, and selflessness as selflessness, rightly grasping their object — this is called undistorted perception, undistorted mind, and undistorted view.

items.title: Section: Five Kinds of Discrimination Complete Perception — And Formations' Own Five-Angle Analysis Begins

items.zh: 別。分別差別者，略有五種想分別相。一、境界分別，二、領納分別，三、假設分別，四、虛妄分別，五、實義分別。若於境界取隨味相，名境界分別。執取境界所生諸受，名領納分別。若於自他，取如是名、如是類、如是姓等種種世俗言說相，名假設分別。於諸境界取顛倒相，名虛妄分別。於諸境界取無倒相，名實義分別。如是總名想蘊分別差別。復次，云何行蘊差別？亦由五相。一、由境界故；二、由分位故；三、由雜染故；四、由清淨故；五、由造作故。
items.en:
Fifth, discrimination; first, distinguishing it; first, stating and listing. Discrimination is, in brief, of five kinds: discrimination of the object, of reception, of designation, born of delusion, and of true meaning.
Fourth, formations' distinctions; first, the question posed. Furthermore, what are formations' distinctions? Second, the explanation; first, stating and listing. This too is of five aspects: object, phase, defilement, purity, and active construction.

items.title: Section: Formations' Five Angles Complete — Object, Temporal Phase, Defilement, Purity, and Active Construction

items.zh: 由境界者，謂於行蘊立六思身。由分位者，謂立生等不相應行，由彼生等唯有分位所顯現故。由雜染者，謂於雜染諸行建立煩惱及隨煩惱。由清淨者，謂於清淨諸行建立信等。由造作者，謂如前說五造作相，為境隨與等。
items.en:
Fourth, by purity. By purity, formations are established through faith and the other wholesome mental factors cultivated within purified conditioned phenomena.
Fifth, by active construction. By active construction, formations are established through the five aspects already explained: going along with the object, and the rest.

blocks.text: A short day: the four distortions that sit at the heart of the Buddha's diagnosis, and how they grow from perception into mind and view.

Taking the impermanent as permanent, suffering as pleasure, the impure as pure, and what is not self as self. Distorted perception produces a distorted mind in householders, and distorted views in some renunciants. Master Cháng Bǎi: it moves householders to greed, hatred, and delusion.

Wrongly grasping the mark is distorted perception; craving the object through it is distorted mind; clinging to it, endorsing and teaching it, is distorted view. (Untranslated, 0594c01: "this is called the distinction of non-distortion.")
Of the object, of reception, of designation, of delusion, and of true meaning. Master Cháng Bǎi: the ordinary mind constantly discriminates falsely and does not know it.
Arising, ageing, abiding, and impermanence are set up on the changing phases of body and mind.
Karma and vows, two deep attainments, and the five aggregates analysed again. The four distortions at the end are the root of it all: perception goes wrong first, then mind, then view.

quiz.q: What does distorted perception give rise to, and in whom?
options: in householders distorted view; in a portion of renunciants distorted mind
in all renunciants distorted mind; in all householders distorted perception
in householders distorted mind; in a portion of renunciants distorted view
only outsiders have distorted view, and no Buddhist disciples
quiz.why: The treatise says distorted perception gives rise to distorted mind among householders, and to distorted view among a portion of renunciants. Master Cháng Bǎi: it moves householders to the distorted mind of greed, hatred, and delusion, chasing the five desires; not truly knowing saṃsāra and nirvāṇa, and producing pride and mistaken ideas, is distorted view.

quiz.q: How do distorted perception, mind, and view differ?
options: wrongly grasping the mark of the four objects is perception; craving attachment to the object is mind; clinging to, endorsing, teaching, and establishing it is view
craving attachment is perception; wrongly grasping the mark is mind; clinging is view
clinging is perception; craving attachment is mind; wrongly grasping is view
all three mean the same, differing only in lay and monastic usage
quiz.why: The treatise separates three stages: wrongly grasping the mark of the four objects is distorted perception; craving attachment to the object through this apprehension is distorted mind; clinging to, endorsing, teaching, and establishing the distortion is distorted view. Master Cháng Bǎi: explaining wrong views to others and building doctrines on them is distorted view.

quiz.q: What are the five kinds of perception's discrimination?
options: discrimination of the object, of temporal phase, of defilement, of purity, and of active construction
discrimination of substance, characteristic, arising, contemplation, and liberation
discrimination of the object, of reception, of designation, born of delusion, and of true meaning
discrimination of substance, characteristic, distortion, non-distortion, and discrimination
quiz.why: The treatise lists discrimination of the object, of reception, of designation, of delusion, and of true meaning. Master Cháng Bǎi: the ordinary mind constantly discriminates falsely, distorted and unaware of it; those who train in or accomplish the noble path can have discrimination of true meaning. The other options are the headings for formations, feeling, and perception as a whole.

quiz.q: 分位 is "temporal stage" for consciousness in §58 and "temporal phase" for formations in §73. According to the lecture, do both concern time?
options: yes: both refer only to past, present, and future, so the English is correct
not both: consciousness's stage is knowing the three times; formations' is the changing phases of body and mind, on which dissociated formations are set, so "temporal" is too narrow
neither: both refer to stages of practice, and the English should say so
neither: both refer to the number of mental factors, and the English should say so
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the distinction of stage for consciousness means it can discern past, present, and future, so "temporal" fits there. For formations he explains: on the differing phases of change in body and mind, arising, ageing, abiding, impermanence, and the other twenty-four dissociated formations are established. Those phases are states, not time periods, so "temporal phase" is too narrow.
